brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer (notch drawer frame) at the very same corner of the same cell as the spike
requirements.evidence: piece:1,0,0;full is the shared cell. Spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 sits at junction [0,0 + 0,1 + 1,0] – one corner of piece:1,0,0. Notch drawer frame notch:0#1,1#notch2 at q1,r1 k2 is seated in the empty cell between piece:0,1,0 and piece:1,0,0, wrapping the same corner of piece:1,0,0. Both coexist with meshClash clear and are visibly touching in overhead view.

requirements.requirement: One spike at the same corner, touching the drawer
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 placed at same junction as above, coexists with the notch frame with no clash; check_build ok, look from above shows adjacency/touching.

finish.summary: Built 3-cell cluster (0,0, 1,0, 0,1) to create the shared three-cell junction. Placed spike at level 0 junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 and notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) in empty cell 1,1 k2 spanning 0,1–1,0, so both occupy the same corner of cell 1,0,0 and touch. House rules applied (capOpenFaces, lockJoints), verified clear.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
